description: Defines the canonical TEL grammar. TEL is a formal notation system for encoding AI Edition structural configurations, transformations, constraints, and invariant assertions. All TEL expressions must conform to this grammar before evaluation.

rules.note: Top-level production. Every well-formed TEL expression reduces to one of these five forms.
Irreducible terminal expression. Corresponds to a single AI Edition primitive (node, relation endpoint, or declared constant).
Binary composition. Parentheses are mandatory and non-optional. Nesting depth is unbounded.

semantics.⊕: Relational union — combines two structure sets under shared relational closure
semantics.⊗: Relational product — cross-product of two relation sets with shared constraint application
semantics.→: Directed structural dependency — left structure depends on right
semantics.⊢: Constraint assertion — left structure must satisfy right constraint expression
semantics.⊥: Structural disjointness — left and right share no relational elements

rules.note: Encodes a named transformation mapping an input structural expression to an output structural expression.
Declares a named constraint over a TEL expression. The constraint is evaluated by TEL-Α (Assert) in the assert phase.
Top-level invariant assertion. Must reference a declared invariant identifier. Evaluated strictly by TEL-Α.
Uppercase alphanumeric string with underscores/hyphens. Case-sensitive. Must match a declared entity in the active AI Edition module registry.

Primitive value literals. Numeric literals may be integer or real. Booleans are ⊤ (true) and ⊥ (false) — note ⊥ is overloaded: as compose_op it means disjointness; as boolean literal it means false. Context resolves the reading.
Reference to a declared symbol in the active TEL scope. Symbols are declared via prior INV or C expressions in the same evaluation session.

well_formedness_rules: WF-001: Parentheses must be balanced. Unmatched parentheses constitute a parse error.
WF-002: All identifiers must resolve to declared entities in the active module registry. Unresolved identifiers constitute a syntax error, not a runtime error.
WF-003: T[…] expressions must have exactly one '→' at the top level of the transform body.
WF-004: INV[…] expressions must reference an invariant declared in the active book's invariants file.
WF-005: Nesting of INV[…] inside T[…] or C[…] is not permitted at the grammar level.
WF-006: The ⊥ token is resolved as compose_op when appearing between two <tel_expression> terminals inside parentheses; otherwise as boolean literal.
